topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture scope on the initiation, cellular mechanisms, and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of pathogen and damage recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects infection and tissue injury by recognizing conserved molecular patterns through germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor localization and signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the structure, cellular distribution, and intracellular signaling cascades of Toll-like receptors in generating distinct antimicrobial responses.

topics.label: Cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptors and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine intracellular sensing mechanisms, focusing on Nod-like receptors and the assembly of inflammasome complexes required for activating pro-inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the progression from sentinel cell activation and leukocyte extravasation into tissues to lymphatic drainage and the pathological risks of excessive systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that shut down inflammation and coordinate tissue repair, alongside the chronic pathology and granuloma formation that occur when resolution is incomplete.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and provides a forward reference to the upcoming topic.
